svg.title: Governed recall pipeline
svg.desc: A mobile-first governed recall pipeline. A query resolves requester, purpose, and scope before candidate generation. Retrieval may be probabilistic, but candidates are normalized with provenance and policy-relevant metadata, then explicitly admitted or rejected using identity, tenancy, purpose, scope, sensitivity, destination, consent or delegation, certification or dispute state, freshness, and policy. Ranking happens only among admitted candidates. Composition risk and context budget checks occur before assembly, and consequential recall emits an explanation or receipt. High relevance is not permission, and a prohibited candidate never becomes admitted through randomness.
svg.text: Governed recall pipeline
Retrieval finds candidates. Admission decides what may enter context.
HARD INVARIANT
high relevance != authorized recall
Candidate generation may be probabilistic. Admission and scope
enforcement are explicit and bounded.
A blocked candidate never becomes admitted solely through randomness.
01 QUERY / TASK
Resolve the recall request
Bind requester identity, agent identity, purpose, tenant, destination,
and requested scope before deciding what context is reachable.
Storage permission != universal context permission.
02 CANDIDATE GENERATION
Find potentially useful memory
A planner may combine exact identity lookup, graph traversal, temporal
lookup, evidence search, semantic/vector retrieval, procedural recall,
prospective memory, policy memory, failure memory, and source-aware search.
Ordering or retrieval scores may be probabilistic.
No retrieval mode owns truth or authority.
03 CANDIDATE NORMALIZATION
Preserve what policy needs to know
memory identity · retrieval method/version · score type/value/uncertainty
source scope · memory scope · sensitivity · dispute state
certification state · freshness · provenance references
A score must say what it means.
Similarity, confidence, source trust, saturation, and policy priority
remain different signals.
Normalization must not erase scope, sensitivity, dispute, or provenance.
04 RECALL ADMISSION
Permission gate before context inclusion
Evaluate
requester identity · agent identity · tenant · purpose · memory scope
sensitivity · destination · consent/delegation · certification/dispute
freshness · policy version
Possible outcomes
admit · admit_with_warning · admit_redacted · admit_summary_only
require_verification · require_review · quarantine · block
Disputed memory may describe disagreement.
It must not be silently presented as canonical.
Uncertain sensitivity is not non-sensitive.
Wrong-tenant perfect match: block, even at semantic_score = 1.0.
05 RANK ONLY ADMITTED CANDIDATES
Utility comes after permission
Ranking may vary across runs and may use probabilistic utility estimates.
Randomness may choose among admitted candidates only.
A stronger score does not reopen a blocked candidate.
ranking != admission
06 COMPOSITION RISK CHECK
Safe individually can become unsafe together
Check for secret reconstruction, conflicting instructions, unsafe chains,
scope interaction, aggregate sensitivity, and poisoned multi-memory patterns.
Composition may block, transform, or narrow the candidate set.
Admission of individual memories does not waive this second policy boundary.
individually admissible != safe composition
07 CONTEXT BUDGET
Optimize within hard requirements
Budget policy may estimate utility, but it must preserve must-include policy
constraints, required warnings, active correction/dispute state, and critical
procedural prerequisites.
Do not evict the only memory explaining why an action is prohibited.
context pressure != authority to drop governance state
08 GOVERNED CONTEXT ASSEMBLY
Assemble only policy-permitted context
Preserve warnings, redaction or summary-only treatment, temporal state,
dispute/correction semantics, provenance, and destination restrictions.
Context assembly is a governed memory operation.
It is not a vector-search side effect.
09 RECALL RECEIPT / EXPLANATION
Explain consequential recall
why candidate · retrieval method · why admitted · policy version
redaction/transformation · uncertainty/dispute · why stronger scores blocked
The result should make the admission path reconstructable.
retrieval finds candidates · governed recall decides what enters context
Canonical: docs/26-governed-recall-planner.md
Accepted boundary: ADR-013 Governed Recall Planner Is Required
